recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No FHIR-13744 follow-up is needed in core unless a separate work-group decision asks to harmonize newer ResearchStudy introductory prose with the current StructureDefinition wording, which is outside the original duplicate-definition issue.
issue_request: FHIR-13744 was a Published/Persuasive BR&R change request from STU3 asking whether ResearchStudy and ResearchSubject were meant to have the same definition, because both pages used the ResearchStudy definition text. The resolution says the ResearchSubject definition was updated and published in the December 2017 FHIR build.
initial_application: The Jira-tagged commit 62eab837d18ff512a6c5c66549ea653f32b3e38e changed source/researchsubject/researchsubject-spreadsheet.xml for #13744, replacing the copied ResearchStudy short/definition with ResearchSubject-specific wording. That spreadsheet source was later converted into the current StructureDefinition source during build-source refactoring.
additional_context: ResearchStudy and ResearchSubject are active current-build resources in source/fhir.ini and both are assigned to BR&R. Later wording commits for ResearchStudy and ResearchSubject, including FHIR-38076, FHIR-29259/FHIR-31768, and FHIR-50685 source changes, refined the wording without reintroducing a shared definition. Zulip and Confluence searches found no relevant community evidence contradicting the Jira/source/history conclusion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current ResearchStudy StructureDefinition describes a scientific investigation designed to generate health-related knowledge, while the current ResearchSubject StructureDefinition describes a participant or object receiving investigative activities in a research study; the ResearchSubject narrative also uses participant/object wording.
